Quotes / Mary Wollstonecraft / Q0199

English

I do not wish them to have power over men; but over themselves.
Thinker Mary Wollstonecraft
School Feminist Philosophy
Source A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792)
Theme Autonomy
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

This English passage is associated with A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792), within the tradition of Feminist Philosophy. The wording below is a verified rendering prepared for careful reading rather than a claim of unique translation authority.

A short reading

Read in the register of autonomy, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Mary Wollstonecraft's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
